Institutional map

Eight competences, kept apart. Built from the competence edges in the canonical data, each carrying whether it is held exclusively, what it is limited to, and which provision confers it.

Loading the institutional map, with its filters. Until it arrives — or without JavaScript — this is the index of all 21 bodies and their competences:

  • European Commission EU institutionLegislates (across the rulebook: Right of legislative initiative); Issues guidance (across the rulebook); Supervises (DMA, exclusive: Sole enforcer of the DMA); Designates (DMA, exclusive: Gatekeeper designation decisions); Imposes fines (DMA, exclusive); Supervises (DSA: VLOPs and VLOSEs only. National Digital Services Coordinators supervise everything below that tier); Designates (DSA, exclusive: VLOP and VLOSE designation); Imposes fines (DSA: VLOPs and VLOSEs only); Issues guidance (AI Act); Investigates (NIS2: Infringement proceedings against Member States for failure to transpose. Not supervision of entities).
  • DG CONNECT — Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology Directorate-GeneralSupervises (DSA: Houses the Commission’s DSA supervision and enforcement team for designated very large online platforms and search engines (Directorate F, Platforms Policy and Enforcement)); Investigates (DMA: Half of the joint DG COMP–DG CONNECT team responsible for implementing and enforcing the DMA).
  • DG COMP — Directorate-General for Competition Directorate-GeneralInvestigates (DMA: Half of the joint DG COMP–DG CONNECT team responsible for implementing and enforcing the DMA); Investigates (TFEU, exclusive: Article 102 TFEU antitrust enforcement, which runs alongside the DMA rather than instead of it).
  • AI Office — European AI Office EU body or officeSupervises (AI Act, exclusive: General-purpose AI models under Chapter V); Issues guidance (AI Act: Including the GPAI Code of Practice process).
  • EDPB — European Data Protection Board Network of national authoritiesCoordinates (GDPR: Consistency mechanism and dispute resolution between national authorities); Issues guidance (GDPR); Advises (GDPR: Opinions on legislative proposals); Issues guidance (DSA: On the DSA–GDPR interface).
  • EDPS — European Data Protection Supervisor EU body or officeSupervises (GDPR, exclusive: Supervises the EU institutions themselves, under Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 rather than the GDPR); Advises (GDPR: Opinions on legislative proposals, including against the Commission's own).
  • ENISA — European Union Agency for Cybersecurity EU agencyCoordinates (NIS2); Issues guidance (NIS2); Coordinates (CRA: Establishes, manages and maintains the single reporting platform; receives manufacturers' notifications alongside the coordinating CSIRT).
  • CJEU — Court of Justice of the European Union CourtInterprets (across the rulebook, exclusive: Definitive interpretation of Union law, including on preliminary reference); Hears appeals (NIS2, exclusive: Infringement actions against Member States, including financial sanctions).
  • General Court — General Court of the European Union CourtHears appeals (DMA: Actions for annulment against Commission designation and non-compliance decisions); Hears appeals (DSA: Including the supervisory-fee decisions).
  • European Parliament EU institutionLegislates (across the rulebook: Co-legislator under the ordinary legislative procedure).
  • Council — Council of the European Union EU institutionLegislates (across the rulebook: Co-legislator under the ordinary legislative procedure).
  • National DPAs — National data protection supervisory authorities National authoritySupervises (GDPR: Each in its own Member State; cross-border cases are led by the main-establishment authority under the one-stop-shop); Investigates (GDPR); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • Irish DPC — Data Protection Commission (Ireland) National authoritySupervises (GDPR: Lead supervisory authority for most large platform controllers with their main establishment in Ireland); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • AP — Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (Netherlands) National authoritySupervises (GDPR); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • CNPD — Commission nationale pour la protection des données (Luxembourg) National authoritySupervises (GDPR); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • Garante — Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy) National authoritySupervises (GDPR); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • AEPD — Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (Spain) National authoritySupervises (GDPR); Imposes fines (GDPR).
  • Digital Services Coordinators — National Digital Services Coordinators National authoritySupervises (DSA: All intermediaries below the VLOP/VLOSE tier, in the Member State of establishment); Coordinates (DSA: Vetting of researchers and transmission of Art. 40(4) data-access requests).
  • National competent authorities — National competent authorities designated under sectoral instruments National authoritySupervises (Data Act: Enforcement is national and penalties are set by Member States); Supervises (NIS2: Essential and important entities in the Member State); Supervises (CRA: Market surveillance authorities); Supervises (AI Act: AI systems other than general-purpose AI models, which sit with the AI Office).
  • ESAs — European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA, ESMA) EU agencySupervises (DORA: Designate critical ICT third-party service providers through the Joint Committee; the ESA responsible for the financial entities with the largest share of total assets among a provider's users is its Lead Overseer).
  • Member States — Member States of the European Union National authorityTransposes (NIS2, exclusive: Transposition deadline 17 October 2024); Transposes (CER, exclusive: Same transposition deadline); Transposes (Revised PLD, exclusive); Imposes fines (Data Act: Penalty levels are set nationally rather than by the Regulation).

Why the roles are kept apart

Legislating is not supervising, supervising is not fining, and interpreting is neither. Collapsing them into "the EU" is the single most common way this system is misdescribed, and it hides where power actually sits. The Commission legislates, supervises the DSA for VLOPs only, enforces the DMA alone, and issues guidance across the acquis — four different things with four different limits.

Exclusivity matters. A competence marked exclusive has no national route alongside it. The DMA is the clear case: there is no national enforcement path at all.

Where no provision is recorded, the map says so. A competence without a legal basis is an assertion this dataset has not yet anchored, and it is shown as such rather than presented with the same confidence as one that is.
